quests.instruction: A teacher writes the four seasons on the board and asks the class to put them in the order they repeat, starting with spring.
quests.question: Which order is right?
quests.hint: The seasons follow one another in a loop around the year.
quests.explanation: The seasons repeat as spring, summer, autumn and winter, and then spring starts again.
quests.funFact: Seasons happen because Earth is tilted as it travels around the Sun.

quests.instruction: Red, orange and gold leaves are drifting down from the trees in the park.
quests.question: Which season does this usually belong to?
quests.hint: The trees are getting ready for the colder months.
quests.explanation: Many trees drop their leaves in autumn. In some countries this season is called fall, because the leaves fall.
quests.funFact: Leaves turn yellow and orange when their green colouring fades away.

quests.instruction: Mr. Das asks which season has the shortest days in many places.
quests.question: Which season is it?
quests.hint: Daylight hours change gradually through the year.
quests.explanation: In many places, winter has the fewest hours of daylight and summer has the most.
quests.funFact: Near the poles, the summer Sun can stay up for weeks without setting.

quests.instruction: Rina's family notices that after a hot summer, the mornings are getting cooler and the evenings darker.
quests.question: Which change is typical in many places as summer turns to autumn?
options: Snow covers the towns and roads
quests.hint: Remember what happens to daylight after midsummer.
quests.explanation: As autumn arrives, daylight shrinks and average temperatures slowly drop.
quests.funFact: On two days a year, called equinoxes, day and night are nearly equal in length.

quests.instruction: In many places the garden fills with flowers in spring.
quests.question: What helps the flowers bloom?
quests.hint: Plants need warmth, water and light to wake up.
quests.explanation: Spring brings warmer weather, more light and often rain. These help plants grow and flower.
quests.funFact: Some bulbs, such as tulips, need a cold winter before they can bloom in spring.

quests.instruction: In many parts of India, a rainy season called the monsoon arrives each year.
quests.question: What is the monsoon season mostly known for?
quests.hint: Notice what farmers and children both prepare for during this time.
quests.explanation: The monsoon brings steady, often heavy rain that lasts for weeks and refills rivers and fields.
quests.funFact: The word monsoon comes from an Arabic word meaning season.

quests.instruction: It is winter in Canada, but at the same time children in Australia are enjoying summer.
quests.question: Why can two places have opposite seasons at the same time?
options: Australia sits much closer to the Sun
Canada is on the far side of the Moon
Clouds block all the sunlight in the north
Earth's tilt gives them different sunlight
quests.correctAnswer: Earth's tilt gives them different sunlight
quests.hint: Consider how Earth leans as it travels around the Sun.
quests.explanation: Earth is tilted, so when one half leans toward the Sun, the other half leans away. That's why their seasons are opposite.
quests.funFact: Earth is actually closest to the Sun in early January, during winter in the north.

quests.instruction: Kofi lives in a place that is warm all year but has a wet season and a dry season.
quests.question: What does this show about seasons?
options: Seasons do not happen near warm places
All places have the same four seasons
Seasons differ from place to place
All places have snowy winters each year
quests.correctAnswer: Seasons differ from place to place
quests.hint: Ask yourself whether the same pattern could fit every place on Earth.
quests.explanation: Seasons differ around the world. Many warm places divide the year into wet and dry seasons instead of four.
quests.funFact: Many tropical places describe the year as a wet season and a dry season.

quests.instruction: A class debates what winter is like.
quests.question: Which statement is the most accurate?
options: Winter is snowy in some places, mild in others
Winter is snowy in all places on Earth
Winter is dry for everybody everywhere
Winter is warmer than summer in all places
quests.correctAnswer: Winter is snowy in some places, mild in others
quests.hint: Winter doesn't look the same around the world.
quests.explanation: Winter weather depends on where you are. Some places get snow, while others only get cooler, rainy or sunny weather.
quests.funFact: Mount Kilimanjaro, near the equator, has snow near its top.

quests.instruction: Down the street, neighbours are busy outdoors in autumn.
quests.question: Which job is the most typical autumn task in many places?
quests.hint: Imagine what has recently dropped onto lawns.
quests.explanation: Many trees drop their leaves in autumn, so raking is a common job.
quests.funFact: Trees that lose their leaves each autumn are called deciduous trees.

quests.instruction: Farmers in many places sow seeds in spring.
quests.question: Why is spring a good time to plant?
options: The fields are covered in deep snow
The soil warms up and days get longer
It is the driest time of the year
The winds are strongest in spring
quests.correctAnswer: The soil warms up and days get longer
quests.hint: Seeds need the right conditions to wake up and grow.
quests.explanation: Warmer soil, longer days and more moisture help seeds sprout and grow into healthy plants.
quests.funFact: Seeds need both warmth and moisture before they begin to sprout.

quests.instruction: A school records the average daily temperature for each season: winter 3°C, spring 12°C, summer 26°C and autumn 13°C.
quests.question: Which two seasons have the most similar temperatures?
quests.hint: Compare the numbers and look for the closest pair.
quests.explanation: Spring is 12°C and autumn is 13°C, which are much closer to each other than to winter or summer.
quests.funFact: Spring and autumn are often called the in-between seasons.

quests.instruction: Neha says summer days feel longer than winter days.
quests.question: Why do they feel longer?
options: The Sun stays up for more hours
The Sun moves faster in winter
quests.correctAnswer: The Sun stays up for more hours
quests.hint: Focus on when the Sun rises and sets.
quests.explanation: In summer, the Sun rises early and sets late, giving more hours of daylight.
quests.funFact: In northern Norway, the Sun stays up all night around midsummer.

quests.instruction: Over a year, Ava watches a tree outside her window.
quests.question: Which order matches the tree's year in many places, starting in winter?
options: Full green leaves, bare branches, new buds, falling coloured leaves
Falling coloured leaves, full green leaves, new buds, bare branches
New buds, bare branches, falling coloured leaves, full green leaves
Bare branches, new buds, full green leaves, falling coloured leaves
quests.correctAnswer: Bare branches, new buds, full green leaves, falling coloured leaves
quests.hint: Trees follow the season's weather: cold, waking up, warm, cooling.
quests.explanation: Bare branches in winter lead to buds in spring, full leaves in summer and falling coloured leaves in autumn.
quests.funFact: Evergreen trees such as pines keep their needles all year.

quests.instruction: Heavy monsoon rain is forecast for the week. A family packs for a trip.
quests.question: Which items would be the most useful?
options: A sun umbrella and light sandals
quests.hint: Remember staying dry and drying out afterwards.
quests.explanation: In steady heavy rain, rain protection and clothes that dry quickly make the trip much more comfortable.
quests.funFact: Rice crops need a lot of water, so monsoon rains matter for many farms.

quests.instruction: It is summer in both a mountain village and a seaside town, but the village feels much cooler.
quests.question: What could explain the difference?
options: Summer feels the same in all places
Mountains are closer to the Sun's heat
Height and the sea change the weather
Seas get colder at night than land does
quests.correctAnswer: Height and the sea change the weather
quests.hint: Notice where each place is, not just what season it is.
quests.explanation: Air gets cooler as you go higher up a mountain, and seas change how warm a nearby town feels.
quests.funFact: The air usually gets cooler as you climb higher up a mountain.

quests.instruction: Many trees in cooler regions drop all their leaves before winter.
quests.question: Why do they do this?
options: To save water and energy in the cold months
Because birds peck them off one by one
Because the winter wind pulls them off
Because the leaves freeze solid in autumn
quests.correctAnswer: To save water and energy in the cold months
quests.hint: Consider what leaves need to work well.
quests.explanation: Leaves lose water and need sunlight to work. Dropping them helps the tree get through the cold, dark months.
quests.funFact: A large tree can release hundreds of litres of water through its leaves on a hot day.

quests.instruction: A weather presenter describes a typical spring day in many places.
quests.question: Which description fits best?
quests.hint: Spring is the in-between season, not the coldest or hottest.
quests.explanation: Spring weather is often changeable, with mild days, showers and sunny spells.
quests.funFact: Spring can be changeable because warm and cold air keep meeting.

quests.instruction: A town's rainfall chart shows January 10 mm, April 40 mm, July 300 mm and October 80 mm.
quests.question: What does the chart suggest?
options: Snow falling in the month of January
Steady rain through the whole year
quests.hint: Compare each month with the others.
quests.explanation: July's 300 mm is far more than the other months, which points to a wet season around mid-year.
quests.funFact: A wet season can bring more than half of a place's rain in only a few months.

quests.instruction: In the northern half of the world, a class wants to know which month has the longest daytime.
quests.question: Which month is it?
quests.hint: Picture when the Sun is up for the most hours.
quests.explanation: In the northern half of the world, June has the most daylight. In the southern half it's the opposite.
quests.funFact: The longest day of the year is called the summer solstice.

quests.instruction: A class in a snowy region wants to plan a day trip to play in the snow.
quests.question: When should they plan it?
quests.hint: Snow needs very cold air to stay frozen.
quests.explanation: Mid-winter is the coldest time, so snow is most likely to be on the ground.
quests.funFact: In some cold places, snow can still fall in spring.

quests.instruction: The weather changes from the hot days of summer to the cooler days of autumn.
quests.question: How do seasons usually change?
options: All at once on a single day
At midnight on a fixed date each year
On days when it happens to rain
Slowly, with warm and cool days mixed in
quests.correctAnswer: Slowly, with warm and cool days mixed in
quests.hint: Imagine how one warm day can be followed by a cooler one.
quests.explanation: Seasons change slowly. Some days feel like the old season and some like the new, until the pattern settles.
quests.funFact: Weather forecasters often group the year into seasons by months for neat record keeping.

quests.instruction: Dev says that seasons form a cycle.
quests.question: Why are seasons called a cycle?
options: They change with each phase of the Moon
They happen one time in history
They repeat in the same order every year
quests.correctAnswer: They repeat in the same order every year
quests.hint: A cycle goes around and comes back to the start.
quests.explanation: After winter comes spring again, and the pattern repeats every year.
quests.funFact: Earth takes about 365 days to travel once around the Sun.

quests.instruction: A student makes four statements about seasons, and only one is not always true.
quests.question: Which claim is NOT always true?
options: Many places have longer summer days
quests.hint: Look for the word that leaves no room for exceptions.
quests.explanation: Many places, such as warm regions, never see snow in winter.
quests.funFact: Some deserts have cold winter nights but little or no snow.

quests.instruction: During the heavy monsoon, the school bus is delayed again.
quests.question: Why can travel be slow in heavy monsoon rain?
options: Roads flood and visibility is poor
Roads get so hot that tyres stick
Rivers freeze over across the roads
Wind lifts the roads off the ground
quests.correctAnswer: Roads flood and visibility is poor
quests.hint: Focus on how heavy rain affects roads and what drivers can see.
quests.explanation: Heavy rain can flood streets and make it hard to see, so vehicles must go slowly.
quests.funFact: Monsoon downpours can flood city streets in only a few hours.

quests.instruction: A teacher says there are two days a year when day and night are nearly equal.
quests.question: What are these days called?
quests.hint: The name comes from a word meaning equal night.
quests.explanation: On the spring and autumn equinoxes, daytime and night-time are close to the same length.
quests.funFact: The word equinox comes from Latin words meaning equal night.

quests.instruction: A fruit seller says that some fruits are in the market only at certain times of year.
quests.question: Why does this happen?
options: Rain turns every fruit ripe on the same day
Each plant has its own best conditions
Every fruit ripens at the same time everywhere
Farmers keep the fruit in the dark until it ripens
quests.correctAnswer: Each plant has its own best conditions
quests.hint: Remember the weather each plant needs.
quests.explanation: Plants ripen when the weather and daylight suit them, so different fruits are ready in different seasons.
quests.funFact: Mango harvests in many parts of India happen mostly in the warm months.

quests.instruction: A traveller expects autumn weather: 12°C, showers and gusty wind.
quests.question: What should be packed?
options: A heavy snowsuit and ski boots
A sun hat and light sandals
quests.hint: Match the clothes to the temperature and the rain.
quests.explanation: Layers cope with cool temperatures, and a raincoat keeps showers and wind out.
quests.funFact: Autumn weather in many places can change quickly during the day.

quests.instruction: Mr. Das wants an example of something that really shows the season changing, not just the weather of one hour.
quests.question: Which example fits?
options: Wind blowing hard for an hour
A rain shower falling at midday
A cloud passing over the school
quests.hint: A season lasts for weeks or months, not hours.
quests.explanation: Seasonal changes build up over weeks and months. A shower or a gust is a short-term change in the weather.
quests.funFact: A season lasts about three months, while weather can change in hours.

quests.instruction: Anaya is about to pack for a trip abroad and doesn't know the place well.
quests.question: What should she check first?
options: What colour her suitcase happens to be
How many clouds are above her home
The usual weather there that time of year
How much umbrellas cost in the shops
quests.correctAnswer: The usual weather there that time of year
quests.hint: The right clothes depend on what the weather is usually like there.
quests.explanation: Knowing the usual weather and season in a place helps you pack the right clothes.
quests.funFact: Many travel guides suggest the best months to visit based on the seasons.
